plan: With value $3 and 2 competitors, this is a first-price-style auction. Optimal strategy in a symmetric first-price auction with n bidders uniform on [0,49] is to bid (n-1)/n of value. With n=3, bid ≈ 2/3 × 3 = $2. This balances winning probability against overpaying, maximizing expected profit given low value.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, which shades the bid to balance win probability against overpayment. With value $24 and n=3, optimal bid ≈ 24 * (2/3) = $16. This maximizes expected profit by avoiding overbidding while maintaining a competitive chance to win.

With 3 bidders and independent private values uniform on $0-$49, the optimal first-price auction bidding strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, i.e., 2/3 of my value, to maximize expected profit. My value is $11, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 * 11 = $7.3. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin if I win.
